about: Every source the F/A-18C build draws on (claude/plans/air-fa18c.md). use: trace = may be traced and matched; facts = its facts may be cited, its figures are never traced into the repository; look = looked at only. Photos (dvids*) are of the reference airframe, BuNo 164718, unless their aircraft says otherwise. fetch.py downloads each entry with a url into references/ and checks its hash.

aircraft.location: off the coast of San Diego, California, US

references.shows: Left (port) side, front three-quarter: roughly 30-40 deg ahead of abeam, roughly 20-25 deg above the wing plane, jet close to wings-level. Upper surfaces of both wings: port wing nearest, fully in frame, its tip trailing corner clear beside the LAU-7/AIM-9 rail; starboard wingtip and its trailing corner visible beyond the canopy. Port horizontal tail fully visible with its tip corner, clear of the fuselage. Starboard horizontal tail mostly hidden by the fuselage: only a small part shows between the two fins, not its tip corner.
references.note: in flight, gear up, surfaces near neutral: for the wing's and the horizontal tails' heights (task #16). A two-seat D: its canopy is not the C's, so no canopy point is marked on it. Gear up, probe retracted. Port wing: TEF and aileron lie flush with the wing, no visible droop. Starboard wing: a small step in the trailing edge at the fold line, with the inboard TEF a few degrees below the outboard aileron (AUTO flap schedule at formation speed, or a roll input). Neither is anywhere near the 30-45 deg ground droop. LEFs show no separate hinge line or droop. Port horizontal tail shows no obvious deflection.
